measured: the fork's tool list must match the parent's or the cache misses entirely. Same tools: cache_read 35,534 / cache_creation 3,550. tools: []: cache_read 0 / cache_creation 44,268. So fork_self's 'no tools' default keeps the tools in the prompt and refuses every call with a PreToolUse hook.

decision.chose: registry liveness by host process: every row carries boot (id minted per host process) + pid + last_at. registry_list() buries rows whose pid is dead (or this process but not in live); revive() at Servex boot reopens rows the previous boot left open within 30 min and buries the rest as gone.
decision.alternative: sweep every non-live row in registry_list() as the brief first said: a standalone host (demo.mjs, fork-proof) shares registry.json and would have marked Servex's own live agents gone

decision.chose: revive in process: at boot Servex re-spawns each revivable row with resume = its session, the same id/parent/role/model/effort/cwd/permission mode; a mid-turn one is told 'Servex restarted mid-turn'. ~60 lines in Agents.js, one call in Servex.js.
decision.alternative: run each agent out of process (one node child per agent that reconnects to Servex): survives a restart without losing the in-flight turn at all, but a new process model, a reconnect protocol and a second place tokens and logs flow through — a bigger change, worth it only if a lost in-flight tool call proves costly

assign.outcome:
**Agents can now fork themselves, wait on each other, and survive a Servex restart.** Merged into michael/dev as 230171d5, plus b6c5d5c0 (restart guard); goes live with this restart.

- **fork_self**: an agent asks a copy of itself one question in the background. Measured: the call returned in 7 ms, the agent answered another message 3 s later while the fork ran, and the fork's answer arrived at 19.5 s. 98% of the fork's input (42,056 tokens) came from the cache, so it cost $0.014. Trap: a fork given different tools reads 0 from the cache, so forks keep the parent's tools. [proof.txt](/framework/ai/2026-09-24/concurrency/proof.txt)
- **wait_for_agent**: returns when an agent ends its turn, so a VS Code tab gets a direct done.
- **spawn_agent resume / fork**: reopen or copy any session. A message to a stopped agent reopens it (wake on message), so idle agents can be stopped to save memory. [wake-proof.txt](/framework/ai/2026-09-24/concurrency/wake-proof.txt)
- **Survive a restart**: at boot, agents from the last Servex come back under the same id, and mid-turn ones are told to check and continue. Dead ones show gone, never idle. sustain --restart now waits only for agents that would not come back. [revive-proof.txt](/framework/ai/2026-09-24/concurrency/revive-proof.txt)
- **start_job**: node does file reads, greps, log watches, syntax checks and one-question decisions, and answers as a message. Every job returned in 0 to 2 ms. [jobs-proof.txt](/framework/ai/2026-09-24/concurrency/jobs-proof.txt)
- **Also**: restart_servex, pause_dispatch and resume_dispatch tools; roles.js is one table; caller identity on every tool call; context size on every card.
